title: Adaptive exemplar holdout calibration bundles for verticalized production prompts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As we expand INT8/FP8 support across our model catalog, calibration dataset selection for production prompts must preserve per-vertical distributional characteristics while limiting label leakage into holdouts. Existing reservoir and stratified samplers produce representative packs but do not explicitly ensure exemplar holdouts (for regression detection) or preserve multi-turn context groups for chat-like prompts.

Goal: Design and deliver an automated pipeline that generates per-vertical calibration bundles with: (1) exemplar holdout sets for regression detection, (2) context-preserving shard grouping (maintain convo continuity), (3) importance-weighted sampling across recency, token-length, and rarity, and (4) lightweight synthetic augmentation to increase coverage of low-frequency intents. The output will feed our INT8/FP8 quantization calibration jobs and offline accuracy validators, and be stored with audit metadata for reproducibility.
sampling_strategy_summary: Pipeline selects traffic slices per vertical, clusters by conversation fingerprint, ranks clusters by a composite importance score (recency * weight_token_length * rarity_boost * customer_priority), then reserves the top N clusters as exemplar holdouts (default 5% of cluster-level traffic). The remaining clusters are sampled with stratified reservoir within vertical/intent bins to target diversity. Synthetic augmentation applies paraphrase and entity-variation templates only to low-frequency intents to reach minimum exemplar counts without skewing natural distribution.
acceptance_criteria: Per-vertical bundles produced for 6 pilot verticals with target sizes between 2k and 20k examples as configured
Exemplar holdouts must be reproducible given seed and include cluster-level metadata (cluster_id, fingerprint, seed, sample_reason)
Offline INT8/FP8 calibration runs show coverage metric >= 90% of unique intents seen in live traffic for each vertical
Regression harness detects at least one injected perturbation in holdout exemplars during test runs
Data pipeline metadata written to s3 with checksums, manifest, and Confluence link for each bundle
tasks: Define vertical list and traffic query templates (BigQuery) — owner: Kai
Implement cluster fingerprinting (conversation-shingle) and group-by pipeline — owner: ML infra
Compute composite importance score and tuning knobs (recency half-life, rarity boost factor) — owner: Applied ML
Holdout selection module with deterministic seeding and export manifest — owner: Kai
Stratified reservoir sampler for remaining clusters with per-intent min quotas — owner: Data Eng
Synthetic augmentation module (paraphrase + entity swap) with sampling rate config — owner: NLU
Integration tests: reproduce bundles locally, run INT8/FP8 calibrations on sample models and send results to dashboard — owner: Eng QA
Documentation: Confluence write-up + schema for manifests + privacy checklist — owner: Asha
validation_plan: Offline metrics: compute KL divergence, token-level logit delta, and top-1 response exact-match between FP16 baseline and INT8/FP8 calibrations on each bundle
Regression tests: inject synthetic label drift and ensure holdout-based detectors flag regressions within configured thresholds
Coverage checks: fraction of unique intents/slots in bundle vs production sample >= configurable threshold (default 0.9)
Bias checks: report per-tenant skew, flag any tenant >5x overrepresentation
End-to-end smoke: deliver a bundle to runtime-1.22 quant calibrator and validate no pipeline failures
implementation_notes: Key design points: cluster at conversation-level so short utterances tied to same session are not split across holdout/training; use deterministic hashing with namespace salt for reproducing cluster assignments; importance score uses exponentially decayed recency (half-life configurable), normalized token-length factor, and rarity computed from inverse-document-frequency over recent 90-day window. Synthetic augmentation is gated: only apply when intent frequency < min_examples and ensure augmented examples are labeled as "synthetic" in manifest. All exports include 'origin' tags (live | augmented | replay) and an anonymized user_id hash. Store manifests in s3://redwood-calibration/verticals/<vertical>/bundles/<bundle_id>/manifest.json
open_questions: What is the canonical vertical taxonomy? (PM to confirm final list and mapping rules)
What minimum holdout fraction should we enforce for small verticals (<2k weekly examples)?
Do we allow synthetic augmentation for payment/PII-sensitive verticals? (security review?)
Should exemplars be single-turn only or allow multi-turn context up to 8 turns?
